title: Interactive cis-QTL browsing with run_cis_qtl_browser
text: run_cis_qtl_browser() launches Shiny application browsing tensorQTL cis-association results one gene time: pick gene, pick one cis-SNPs, see genotype effect plot, underlying linear model summary, filterable table every association tested gene. interactive complement readTQTL() plotGenotypeEffect(): rather writing pairs[pairs$gene_name == ...] hand gene interest, app puts searchable gene list SNP dropdown front data.
code: library(tQTLExperiment)

title: Interactive cis-QTL browsing with run_cis_qtl_browser
text: run_cis_qtl_browser() needs two things: tqe: tQTLExperiment genotype data attached (can extract phenotype genotype vectors plot model), cis_gr: GRanges cis-association results, typically pairs element returned readTQTL(..., mode = "cis_nominal"), metadata columns identifying gene, SNP, phenotype, nominal p-value row (gene_col, snp_col, phenotype_col, pval_col – defaults match readTQTL()’s annotateTensorQTLResults()’s output). vignette reuses pre-computed MAGE chr17 demo results main vignette, need tensorQTL installation: gene_symbol added annotateTensorQTLResults(), run_cis_qtl_browser()’s default gene_col expects: full tqe (genotype-attached) construction used , see main vignette’s “Building tQTLExperiment” section, builds tqe CSHLvc2026::mageSEfilt cached MAGE chr17 PLINK files via tQTLExperimentFromRSE().

title: Interactive cis-QTL browsing with run_cis_qtl_browser
text: pval_thresh applied , front, cis_gr app UI built – fixed filter whole result set, interactive control app . Leave NULL (default) browse every tested pair.
code: if (!requireNamespace("CSHLvc2026")) BiocManager::install("vjcitn/CSHLvc2026") library(CSHLvc2026)  plink_paths <- cache_mage_chr17_plink() plpre <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(plink_paths[["bed"]])  data(mageSEfilt, package = "CSHLvc2026") cd <- as.data.frame(colData(mageSEfilt)) mm <- model.matrix(~ batch + population + sex, data = cd) mm <- mm[, -1, drop = FALSE]  tqe <- tQTLExperimentFromRSE(     se              = mageSEfilt,     plinkPrefix     = plpre,     covariateMatrix = mm,     genome          = "hg38" ) tqe <- addGeneSymbols(tqe)  newpairs <- annotateTensorQTLResults(res$pairs)  # only show associations at pval_nominal <= 0.05 run_cis_qtl_browser(tqe, newpairs, pval_thresh = 0.05)

title: Interactive cis-QTL browsing with run_cis_qtl_browser
text: sidebar : Gene symbol: searchable dropdown (selectizeInput) every distinct value gene_col cis_gr (p-value filter), cis-SNP: repopulated whenever gene changes, listing gene’s distinct SNPs (snp_col), sorted nominal p-value, Plot: explicit action button – genotype-effect plot model summary (re)render clicked, every dropdown change, selecting gene SNP doesn’t trigger two redraws. Three tabs share current gene/SNP selection: Genotype effect: beeswarm plot plotGenotypeEffect(), phenotype value genotype (0/1/2 alternate alleles), selected phenotype-SNP pair. Regression model: summary(lm(phenotype ~ genotype + <covariates>)) pair, printed verbatim – model qtlRegressionStats() fits per pair, shown full rather reduced tidy table. Useful checking covariate significance residual behavior behind specific point. cis associations: DT::datatable() every row cis_gr selected gene (ignoring SNP dropdown), sorted nominal p-value, per-column filters (filter = "top") narrowing hand.

title: PCA exploration of cis-QTL t-statistics with qtlPCABrowser
text: qtlPCABrowser() launches Shiny application runs PCA per-covariate t-statistics produced qtlRegressionStats() set SNP-gene pairs, lets explore result interactively: PCA scatter tab (plotly) selectable PC axes; hovering point shows beeswarm pair’s gene expression genotype, panel right, optionally colored sample-level covariate, PC pairs tab, base-R pairs() plot first five PCs. row t-statistic matrix one SNP-gene pair column one covariate term, PC1/PC2 matrix summarize pairs differ pattern covariate effects driving association – useful spotting pairs whose signal dominated batch population effect rather genotype.
code: library(tQTLExperiment) library(SummarizedExperiment)

title: PCA exploration of cis-QTL t-statistics with qtlPCABrowser
text: already wide qtlRegressionStats() result – instance every gene region, computed ahead time possibly parallel – pass res; gene-symbol selector skipped app opens directly combined PCA. res must contain phenotype_id variant_id columns (wide, t_only = TRUE shape qtlRegressionStats() returns default).
code: symbols <- na.omit(unique(mcols(rowRanges(tqe))[["gene_name"]])) res_list <- lapply(symbols, function(s)     tryCatch(qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = s), error = function(e) NULL)) res_all <- do.call(rbind, res_list) qtlPCABrowser(res_all, tqe = tqe)

title: PCA exploration of cis-QTL t-statistics with qtlPCABrowser
text: PCA, qtlPCABrowser() runs collapseFactorTstats() res (gene’s freshly computed result), using collapse_patterns argument – default tuned MAGE dataset’s factor_batch_* population* dummy columns. keeps factor many levels dominating PCA way qtlRegressionStats() alone , since otherwise contribute one raw t-statistic column per level. Pass collapse_patterns list covariates use different names – see ?collapseFactorTstats. PCA stats::prcomp() resulting t-statistic matrix, centered scaled (center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE), columns naturally larger t-statistics – typically genotype – dominate leading PCs, usually point.
code: qtlPCABrowser(     tqe,     collapse_patterns = list(         site = "^t\\.site",         sex  = "^t\\.sex"     ) )

title: Per-pair regression statistics with qtlRegressionStats
text: Two arguments control shape result: t_only: TRUE (default) returns just t-statistic (estimate / std.error) per term; FALSE also returns estimate, standard error, raw t-statistic, p-value. wideFormat: TRUE (default) pivots one row per pair, one (two, t_only = FALSE) columns per model term; FALSE returns long tidy form, one row per pair x term. wide, t_only = TRUE form exactly qtlPCABrowser() collapseFactorTstats() expect input: one row per SNP-gene pair, one <term>.t column per covariate.

title: Per-pair regression statistics with qtlRegressionStats
text: covariate matrix includes multi-level factor (e.g. batch population), model.matrix() expands several dummy columns, wide qtlRegressionStats() output carries one t.<var><level> column per level. collapseFactorTstats() replaces group single root-mean-square summary column, keeps PCA t-statistics dominated however many levels factor happens . MAGE chr17 dataset used main vignette, covariate matrix includes factor_batch_* population* dummy columns, collapseFactorTstats() reduces group t.batch t.population. See ?collapseFactorTstats pattern arguments.

title: eQTL mapping with tQTLExperiment and tensorQTL
text: tQTLExperiment wraps tensorQTL GPU-accelerated eQTL mapping tool SummarizedExperiment-style container. key design principle two-step workflow keeps R Python separate environments: prepareTQTL() — writes phenotype covariate files directory returns complete python -m tensorqtl command string. user runs command terminal tensorQTL installed. readTQTL() — reads output files back R GRanges. avoids R/Python environment conflicts (conda PATH issues, rpy2 segfaults, duplicate OpenMP runtimes). Genotype data represented lazily via BEDMatrix — PLINK .bed file never loaded R memory. makes practical work whole-genome genotype files containing millions variants.

code: if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))     install.packages("BiocManager") BiocManager::install("vjcitn/tQTLExperiment") pip install tensorqtl

title: eQTL mapping with tQTLExperiment and tensorQTL
text: tensorQTL requires numeric covariates. build model matrix colData using model.matrix(), drop intercept column — tensorQTL expect one. Dropping first column construction (rather using ~ 0 + ...) preserves reference-level dummy coding factor variables.
code: cd <- as.data.frame(colData(mageSEfilt)) mm <- model.matrix(~ batch + population + sex, data = cd) mm <- mm[, -1, drop = FALSE]   # remove (Intercept)

title: eQTL mapping with tQTLExperiment and tensorQTL
text: prepareTQTL() writes pheno.bed covariates.tsv outDir returns shell command. built---maf_threshold flag one tensorQTL’s key advantages — pre-filtering step required. printed command looks like: Paste terminal tensorQTL conda environment active:
code: outdir <- "~/mage_tqtl_run" dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE)  cmd <- prepareTQTL(     tqe17,     outDir       = outdir,     mode         = "cis_nominal",     mafThreshold = 0.05 ) cat(cmd, "\n") python3 -m tensorqtl /path/to/CCDG_mage_chr17 ~/mage_tqtl_run/pheno.bed \     ~/mage_tqtl_run/tqtl_out --mode cis_nominal --maf_threshold 0.05 \     --window 1000000 -o ~/mage_tqtl_run \     --covariates ~/mage_tqtl_run/covariates.tsv conda activate plink-env KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE <paste command>

text: tensorQTL finishes, load results back R. Passing x = tqe17 propagates genome build gene symbols automatically.

code: if (interactive()) {   # Load MAGE chr17 genotypes and pre-computed tensorQTL results   plink_paths <- cache_mage_chr17_plink(verbose = FALSE)   plpre <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(plink_paths[["bed"]])   data(mageSEfilt, package="CSHLvc2026")   cd <- as.data.frame(colData(mageSEfilt))   mm <- model.matrix(~ factor(batch) + population + sex, data = cd)   mm <- mm[, -1, drop = FALSE]   # remove (Intercept)   tqe <- tQTLExperimentFromRSE(    se              = mageSEfilt,    plinkPrefix     = plpre,    covariateMatrix = mm,    genome          = "hg38"    )   tqe <- addGeneSymbols(tqe)   demd = cache_demo_data()   res <- readTQTL(dirname(demd$parquet), mode = "cis_nominal", x = tqe)   newpairs = res$pairs   newpairs = annotateTensorQTLResults(newpairs)    # Launch browser with p-value filter   run_cis_qtl_browser(tqe, newpairs, pval_thresh = 0.05) }
